notes_meta.headline: A chip and AI-capex rout: Lam fell 11.8% on supply constraints despite beating, and Meta fell 7% on spending, dragging AMD, Intel, Marvell and Astera down 8–11%. Apple broke out to a 52-week high, and Robinhood, SoFi, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Intel and Sandisk all report within five sessions
notes_meta.calendar: Week calendar. Fri Oct 23: iPhone Duo on sale. Tue Oct 27: SoFi (about 7am ET) and Robinhood (5pm ET); SK Hynix also reports. Wed Oct 28: Fed decision, Microsoft (2:30pm PT call), Alphabet (est.) and Apple's Los Angeles event. Thu Oct 29: Amazon (2pm PT call), Intel (2pm PT) and Sandisk. Mon Nov 2: Apple (2pm PT, confirmed) and Palantir. Tue Nov 3: AMD (2pm PT) and Astera; Snowflake Expedition Nov 3–5. Wed Nov 4: Arm and Qualcomm. Thu Nov 5: MP Materials (5pm ET). Pending, no date: Judge Noreika's ruling on Qualcomm's royalty suspension against Arm. Chart picture: LRCX (−11.8%, RSI 6), ALAB (−11.1%), MRVL (−8.7%), SNDK (−8.5%), AMD (−8.1%), INTC (−8.0%), ARM (−7.3%) and META (−7.0%) led a broad breakdown. NVDA, META, AVGO, AMD, MU, INTC, ARM, MRVL, LRCX, ALAB, SNDK and ORCL all closed below their prior 20-day lows, and GOOG did so for a second day. AAPL (+1.2%) closed at a 52-week high, and IBM held its post-earnings breakout. LRCX (6), ARM (10), INTC (12), SNDK (17) and AMD, MU and MP (24) are the most oversold, and IBM (84) and AAPL (72) are the most extended. Gaps: many articles could not be opened, so items are headline only. IBM's close differs between sources ($252.11 IBKR vs $252.66 stockanalysis main page), and OKTA's close came from IBKR only.
